detail.longDescription: I used Homepage for a while and it worked well enough for me but my wife kept saying it didn't work well on mobile or that she wanted to see our security cameras (Frigate), email, or media. I always joke that my wife is my most difficult end user to please, so her actually using it is already a win in my book. I started thinking about how I could just combine the Home Assistant setup we've had for a few years with some practical home server pieces. Then just started thinking it'd be nice to create a place where I could have actionable server items (update containers, read RSS feeds, view cameras, see Dozzle's logs, etc.) all in one place with minimal configuration, so that I could check if backups completed successfully, see problems before they fail silently, and just learn some more. I'm not a "traditional" software engineer, or would even consider myself one at all I suppose. In my current role I've been kind of expected to transition from data analytics/engineering and managing ETL pipelines into more full-stack development work, so I've done a lot of research about agentic coding and guardrails. I spend a while drawing out models, permissions, maps and flows on a whiteboard before ever prompting anything. It's been fun and exciting but even I feel, as a non-developer, that there has to be a lot of work to frame everything correctly to get a tool that's useful, and I'd struggle to ever think anything I whip up should be sold to anyone. Self-hosting and home automations have always been a hobby but AI has helped me create some internal tools at work or home that take existing services or platforms and consolidate them into one view, and that's the framework I applied to this. Demo with fake data: docker run --rm -p 3200:3200 -e DEMO=1 ghcr.io/sourpatchdad/patchboard:latest
